whmBands2026_27.note: Rates and ceilings confirmed against the 2026-27 withholding schedule. The four base amounts are derived rather than published: Schedule 15 gives coefficients and no dollar base, and the ATO assessment page still stops at 2025-26. Schedule 15 is a withholding instrument and the ATO overwrites this URL in place each 1 July, so the citation stops evidencing 2026-27 on 1 July 2027. Re-check the assessment page around June 2027, which is when the base amounts should become publishable.

foreignResidentBands2025_26.note: Annual assessment rates for someone who was a foreign resident for the whole year. No tax-free threshold, since the first band charges 30c from the first dollar, and no Medicare levy. An employer not registered to withhold at working holiday rates withholds at foreign resident rates instead, but that rule and its periodic tables live in Schedule 15 rather than on this page.

noTfnWithholdingRate.note: 45 per cent, not 47. The published 47 per cent applies to a resident payee; Schedule 15 sets a flat 45 per cent for working holiday makers with no residency test. The rate itself is long standing, but this URL is overwritten each 1 July and now serves the version effective 1 July 2026, so the start date recorded here rests on an archived copy of the previous version rather than on the live page.

taxFreeThreshold.note: Income Tax Rates Act 1986 s 3(1). A working holiday maker's working holiday income is taxed under Schedule 7 Part III whatever their residency, so the threshold does not shelter it. What treaty nationality plus residency buys is the right to be assessed on the resident basis where that comes out cheaper, which is a comparison and not a switch. This pack only handles working holiday wages; a resident with other Australian income reaches whatever of the threshold is left over regardless of nationality, because Schedule 7 Part I clause 4 stacks working holiday income underneath it. The 2012 start is evidenced by the year-by-year tables on the ATO resident rates page, where 2012-13 is the first year at 18,200.

medicareLevyRate.note: Two per cent of taxable income. The cited page states the rate and nothing else: the foreign resident exemption is claimed on the return as category 2 and lives under medicare-levy-exemption/foreign-residents-exemption-from-medicare-levy, and the entitlement statement route is on Services Australia. The 2014 start comes from Act No 43 of 2013 and is not on this page either.

daspWhmRates.note: A two-limb test, and the second limb matters. The rate applies where the person has ever held a 417 or 462 or an associated bridging visa AND the payment includes amounts attributable to contributions made while they held it. When held it does not matter; that the contributions fall in that period does. Someone who held a 417 years ago, accrued nothing then, and whose balance is all from a later visa pays the ordinary rates. Once triggered the rate applies to the entire payment with no apportionment. The dedicated tax-rates page for DASP is a 404; the table lives on the topic page cited here, and the 1 July 2017 start is s 5(3)(a) of the Superannuation (Departing Australia Superannuation Payments Tax) Act 2007.

daspOtherTemporaryResidentRates.note: The ATO calls this the ordinary rate. It is displaced entirely rather than blended the moment any working holiday period contribution is in the payment, so the rule name undersells how easily it stops applying. These percentages have been in s 5(1) since 2007, but s 6 raised them to 38 and 47 for the temporary budget repair levy years, which is why the start recorded here is 2017 rather than 2007. Separately, s 5(2) taxes an excess untaxed rollover amount at nil to avoid double taxation, which bites unclaimed super held by the ATO, exactly where a departed backpacker's money often sits.

deductionSubstantiationThreshold.note: No receipts needed below this total, but the expense must actually have been incurred and the taxpayer must be able to explain how the figure was worked out. It is not a free 300 dollars. ITAA 1997 s 900-35 is repealed by Act No 49 of 2026 Sch 4 Pt 1 item 11 for assessments for 2026-27 and later, so this is the last year it applies. From then every dollar of actual work expense needs written evidence under s 900-15, and a resident gets the standard deduction instead.

laundryWrittenEvidenceThreshold.note: Covers washing, drying and ironing but not dry-cleaning. Laundry still counts towards the 300 dollar total. ITAA 1997 s 900-40 is repealed by the same item as s 900-35, so this ends with 2025-26.

laundryPerLoadRates.note: Per load. These are the ATO practice for working out what a laundry claim is worth, not an evidence exception, so the 2026-27 repeal of the written evidence thresholds leaves them standing.

standardWorkDeduction.note: ITAA 1997 s 25-130, inserted by Act No 49 of 2026 Sch 4 Pt 1, applying to assessments for 2026-27 and later. It is not a flat addition: the amount is the lesser of 1,000 and total labour income, reduced by the work deductions actually claimed, so the effect is a floor rather than a bonus and someone claiming more than 1,000 simply gets their actual expenses. Working holiday wages are labour income. The gate is being an Australian resident at any time in the year, with no apportionment for a part-year resident, so a foreign resident gets neither this nor the repealed 300 dollar allowance and is worse off than in 2025-26. No election and no indexation.

residentBands2025_26.note: Identical to 2024-25 in every threshold, rate and base amount. The page prints the 2026-27 table above this one, so read by year and never by position. Base amounts are published for the third band and up; the second band is published only as "16c for each $1 over $18,200", which is a base of zero. Excludes the Medicare levy.

residentBands2026_27.note: The second band drops to 15c. Unlike the working holiday table for the same year these base amounts are published rather than derived. Excludes the Medicare levy.

lowIncomeTaxOffset.note: Non-refundable: it reduces tax payable to zero and no further, and an unused part is not paid out. The ATO page states no income year; ITAA 1997 s 61-110 applies it to 2020-21 and later years and s 61-115 has not been amended since, which is what makes it good for both years here. Available in full to a part-year resident: s 61-110(1)(a) asks only for residency "at any time during the income year", so unlike the tax-free threshold it is not apportioned. Taper reaches zero at 66,666.67 while entitlement ceases above 66,667, so clamp at zero.

medicareLevyLowIncomeSingle2025_26.note: Single with no dependants and no seniors offset. Both comparisons are inclusive: no levy at or below the lower threshold, a reduction at or below the upper one, the full rate only above it. The shade-in rate is not on the ATO site but is stated in Medicare Levy Act 1986 s 7(2) as 10 per cent of the excess, and the worked example on this page pins it exactly, since 29,000 gives 98.90. These thresholds are indexed by an amending Act passed late and applied retrospectively; Act No 58 of 2026 enacted these figures on 30 June 2026 for 2025-26 and later years, so they are technically in force for 2026-27 as well. This pack does not use them for that year, because the indexation rise is legislated afterwards and pre-indexation figures would overstate someone's levy.

partYearTaxFreeThreshold.note: Someone who becomes a resident partway through the year gets 13,464 plus 4,736 apportioned over the months they were a resident, counting the month of arrival in full and running to 30 June. Staying until 30 June does not avoid the apportionment. Whole calendar months, so 31 January and 1 January both count six. Income Tax Rates Act 1986 s 18(1) covers two shapes the ATO page does not: someone who ceases residency mid-year, and arrive-work-leave, where the period runs from the start of the arrival month to the end of the departure month. There is no apportionment at all where the period is the whole year. The formula is an exact fraction with no rounding, so an odd month count leaves cents. In statute only 4,736 and 18,200 are literals and 13,464 is the difference, so if the threshold ever moves the flat component goes stale silently. The page carries no effective date; 2012-07-01 is when the 18,200 threshold began.
